title: Peanut Avoidance Lost To Early Consumption: Diagnoses Later Fell 43%
hook: Peanut diagnoses fell 43% after advice shifted toward early introduction.
closing: Parents should discuss safe early introduction with their child's clinician; prevention advice depends on the child's situation.
question: How did peanut advice change in your family?

segments.say: Childhood peanut allergy prevalence reached 1.4% in the supplied historical series. It had more than tripled from the earliest measurement.
The avoidance group's allergy rate was 13.7% in the trial. Children who ate peanut early had a much lower rate.
Diagnoses declined about 43% in the before-and-after comparison. That decline followed changed guidance; this comparison alone does not isolate its cause.
